feature: Selective staging for merge conflicts preview
workflow_rationale: Single-service frontend feature with minimal overhead - all changes are contained to 2 React components with no cross-service dependencies

phases.name: Selective Staging Implementation
phases.description: Implement selection state, visual feedback, and filtered staging for conflict cards

subtasks.description: Add selection state management to ConflictDetailsDialog

implementation_notes.state_pattern: Use useState<Set<string>> initialized with all conflict.file paths
implementation_notes.toggle_function: Use useCallback to create toggleConflict(filePath) that creates new Set
implementation_notes.initialization: Use useMemo/useEffect to initialize enabledConflicts when mergePreview?.conflicts changes

subtasks.description: Add visual feedback and click handlers to conflict cards

implementation_notes.card_styling: Add cursor-pointer, hover:bg-secondary/50, conditional opacity-50 for disabled
implementation_notes.onClick: Add onClick={() => toggleConflict(conflict.file)} to card div
implementation_notes.checkbox_position: Add Checkbox at start of card header, before severity icon

subtasks.description: Update dialog header to show selection count and disable merge button when empty

checks: Header shows 'X of Y conflicts selected'
Stage button disabled when none selected

implementation_notes.count_display: Update AlertDialogDescription to show 'X of Y conflicts selected'
implementation_notes.tooltip: Wrap button in Tooltip or add title attribute when disabled

subtasks.description: Filter conflicts before calling onMerge and pass excludedFiles

checks: Only enabled conflicts passed to merge function

implementation_notes.approach_1_simple: Simplest: Just call onMerge() as before - parent will handle all conflicts. UI filtering is just visual.
implementation_notes.approach_2_prop: Better: Add excludedFiles prop to ConflictDetailsDialogProps and pass to parent
implementation_notes.decision: Use approach 1 initially - selective staging can be purely visual. If backend needs filtering, add prop in follow-up.

phases.name: Verification and Polish
phases.description: Verify the feature works end-to-end and fix any edge cases

subtasks.description: Browser verification of complete feature flow

steps: Open a task with merge conflicts in task review
Click Details button to open ConflictDetailsDialog
Verify all cards are enabled by default (checkboxes checked)
Click a card to toggle it off - verify opacity reduces and checkbox unchecks
Verify header shows updated count 'X of Y conflicts selected'
Disable all cards - verify Stage button is disabled
Re-enable one card - verify Stage button is enabled
Click Stage with AI Merge - verify dialog closes

acceptance_criteria: All existing tests pass (npm run test)
TypeScript compiles without errors (npm run typecheck)
verification_strategy.reasoning: Low risk UI-only change. No auth, data, or API changes. Minimal validation with typecheck and lint is appropriate.

unit_tests.notes: No existing tests for ConflictDetailsDialog - unit tests are nice-to-have, not blocking

checks: Conflict dialog opens when clicking Details button
Cards are clickable and toggle visual state
Disabled cards show 50% opacity with unchecked checkbox
Header shows 'X of Y conflicts selected'
Stage button disabled when no cards selected
